**Security: pass-with-notes**, delta only, at `83bb002b5751c40d334029d541ce3a8d65a05094`. **The previously reported MEDIUM cutoff race is closed.**

The merge cutoff is certified across selection and the directory write, within the existing documented clock, authority and transaction limits. No remaining delta vulnerability or C19/C21 disclosure found.

| # | Severity | File | Lines | Vulnerability | Confidence |
|---|----------|------|-------|---------------|------------|
| — | — | — | — | No remaining delta finding; prior cutoff TOCTOU closed | — |

## Why the cutoff survives reassignment

`DirectoryService::finished_by` selects only open, eligible project holdings whose parsed `from` is strictly earlier than the GitHub merge time. Every delivered target now carries `from: Some(held.from.clone())`, not just its role/instance/seat (`crates/daemon/src/community/directory.rs:2020-2073`).

Before ending a row, `release_many` matches that same start identity as well as the existing open-seat/instance condition under the writer lock. A release/reassignment between selection and commit leaves the replacement unmatched and explicitly named rather than ended (`directory.rs:1912-1950`). Exact `from` equality preserves the selected cutoff decision; it need not trust the current tuple as the old holding.

`from` is part of the repository's holding identity. Duplicate seat/instance/from rows refuse; the subsequent SQLite update is also keyed by project/role/instance/seat/from (`crates/daemon/src/community/holders.rs:25-54`; `crates/store/src/community.rs:247-270`). Explicit single/batch release deliberately uses an unpinned target and retains its existing management authority; the delivered path does not.

The merge time still comes from the requested PR's `gh pr view` response in the resolved repository. No caller cutoff or PR-body timestamp is introduced. Missing/unparseable merge time leaves holdings alone; equality/later starts remain excluded. The main merge does not remove the repair.

## Proof

CI [42428276067](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42428276067) checked synthetic merge `c0b5d5b`, explicitly incorporating this head. Its JUnit artifact [13595834888](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42428276067/artifacts/13595834888) contains 2,194 passing cases with no failures; the runner separately reports five skipped.

`a_reassignment_between_the_choice_and_the_commit_survives` passed in 0.626 seconds. It drives the actual selection helper, releases and reassigns the same coder key/seat, then invokes the writer on the earlier targets. Only the still-original reviewer ends; the replacement coder remains open in both the store and holders document, and the old target is named as skipped (`crates/daemon/tests/directory_http.rs:6990-7067`). Removing the pin predicate would select that coder and violate these assertions; this is source-based counterfactual reasoning, not a local mutation run.

The sequential reassignment/replay, refused-first-write retry, absent merge time and initial-delivery controls also passed. These tests exercise the phase boundary deterministically, not a live concurrent HTTP/production canary.

## Retained limits

Local and remote heads agree; worktree clean; PR CLEAN and ready; five successful checks, plus an older cancelled Delivers run. Existing GitHub/local-clock skew, accepted timestamp formats, paths-not-completion semantics, any-seat release/F88 authority and Git/SQLite/window transaction split remain documented qualifications, not reopened cutoff findings. ddocs reported UNAVAILABLE.

Direct source/CI delta review. No local builds/tests, installs, credentials, actual releases/delivery, product edits or production/pane/process probes. No unrelated imported-main implementation re-review.
